A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, Figure 1, and complete Appendices A and B are readable and matchable; the additional page in v2 reflects reference expansion and reflow.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B report mechanism constructions, mathematical guarantees, and proofs. Figure 1 illustrates a mathematical identity; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B contain theoretical results and analytical comparisons, with no experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: The coin-toss mechanism, deterministic phases mechanism, and both prediction-window mechanisms retain identical procedures, prices, inputs, and allocation rules in Sections 3–4.

E1.justification: Neither version uses training or evaluation datasets. The theoretical single-item allocation setting, random-order arrivals, and prediction scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The analytical comparisons involving RSOL, the randomized mixture, and the two prediction-window mechanisms are retained. The newly cited works are not introduced as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. The arrival assumptions, prediction-window ranges, and conditions used in the theoretical comparisons remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The robustness analyses and mechanism comparison in Appendices B.2–B.4 are unchanged. No ablations, empirical robustness tests, or additional case studies are introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experiments, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The probability calculations and expected-utility bounds are unchanged theoretical derivations.

E6.justification: The approximation factors, consistency–robustness guarantees, and analytical comparison findings are identical. Theorems 1–5 and Appendix B.4 contain no revised values or added results.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorem and lemma statements, and proofs are unchanged, including both appendices. Removing a stray comma in the coupling argument does not alter its mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim deterministic constant approximation and simultaneous consistency and robustness using predictions identifying the highest-valued agent. The contrasting impossibility for knowing only the highest value is also unchanged.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications remain intact. Both retain the warnings that the comparison concerns non-tight lower bounds, constants are unoptimized, and stronger prediction models and error tolerance remain open directions.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 retains the same disclosure that SymPy assisted algebraic transformations. No implementation details, computational settings, or code/data access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds Berzack et al. (2025, 2026), with corresponding references on dynamic rental games and constrained buyers. Essaidi et al. (2020) becomes its 2024 published entry, retaining the same arXiv identifier; this is an updated existing reference. The substantive positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes a few hyphenation and punctuation edits, updates the document date, and revises bibliographic wording. Section order and almost all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 19 to page 20 with identical image content and caption. The expanded references reflow subsequent appendix pages; there are no new figures, tables, or display redesigns.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves scholarly documentation through additional related-work acknowledgment and published reference details, alongside small copyedits. The mechanisms, mathematical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited to reference completeness and editorial polish.
